hypothesis: Computing the existing score-only sibling ordering estimate from one parent score scan plus exact move deltas preserves the identical search tree while reducing ordering overhead enough to improve wall-clock time.
interpretation: The delta estimator matched the existing score-only estimate exactly for every tested root action, including captures, Crownline scoring, Game 1 and Game 2 geometry, and terminal child states.

Action choice and expanded-node count were identical to score-only ordering at every tested frozen position for depths 2, 3, and 4. This confirms the change altered estimate computation cost only, not search policy or traversal order.
At depth 2 delta ordering remained unable to reduce nodes and was 25.6 percent slower than baseline, but it was 3.5 percent faster than the previous score-only ordering implementation.
At depth 3 delta ordering preserved the 36.2 percent node reduction and was 3.3 percent faster than score-only ordering, but remained 58.4 percent slower than baseline.
At depth 4 delta ordering preserved the 44.0 percent node reduction and was 3.5 percent faster than score-only ordering, but remained 12.8 percent slower than baseline.

The hypothesis is supported narrowly: incremental score deltas reduce ordering overhead without changing the tree. The gain is real but smaller than hoped because ordering overhead is not dominated by child score rescans alone.

The next clean combination is to apply the already-validated structural exact transposition table to this delta-equivalent ordering engine. Relative to the prior combined experiment, that changes only ordering-estimate implementation while preserving the same ordering policy and exact-cache semantics.
